subject: Fscores() and observations with only NAs

messages.author: 571bc49ad5c5fb80
messages.subject: Fscores() and observations with only NAs
parts: I observed that when fscores() is called with argument full.scores=TRUE, values of factor scores (of about 0) are assigned also to observations that have no other value than NA on all variables used in the estimated model. It seems rather inconvenient to me. If regarding EAP or MAP estimators it can be justified as using only information from prior in absence of any new empirical information for these observations, fscores() behaves in the same manner also when ML or WLE estimator is selected. Generally I think that what most users would expected (analogously to most other IRT software) is assigning NAs to such observations (even if using EAP or MAP). Maybe at least a warning should be returned by fscores() if it detect such observations in the data.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fscores() and observations with only NAs
parts:
This is a good point, I'll add the more appropriate NA's to responses with no information. Though just a note, there really is no reason to include these individuals in any part of the analysis since they provide no contribution to the model. So in the mirt() step, they really should just be removed. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: 571bc49ad5c5fb80
messages.subject: Re: Fscores() and observations with only NAs
parts:
Yes, there is no reason to include such individuals in analysis, but sometimes people analyze datasets in which information from multiple measurement tools were joined, and these tools were administered not at the same time. In such a case typically some individuals did not responded to some measurement tools what generates "block" nonresponse in the dataset. People analyzing such a data will typically take it "as is" and put it to mirt "as is" only selecting columns. And in such a case they can be really surprised with a distribution of factor scores :)

Thanks!

Tomek
